British comedy series "Small Prophets" first two episodes now streaming on Apple TV+, following a wave of early praise for the show. Check out the trailer below.

"Small Prophets" now streaming on Apple TV+

Earlier this morning, my colleague Ryan reported on the strong early reviews for "Small Prophets", a British comedy series whose international rights Apple TV+ acquired earlier this year.

The acquisition marks a first for Apple TV+, as the platform has never before purchased an English-language series that had already aired elsewhere.

"Small Prophets" originally premiered earlier this year on BBC iPlayer and BBC Two in the UK, before Apple picked up the international rights back in August.

Apple TV+ subscribers worldwide can now watch the series, with the exception of the UK, where it will arrive on the local service in 2027.

"Small Prophets" is created, written and directed by Mackenzie Crook ("Detectorists"), who also stars. The cast also includes Pearce Quigley ("The Way Back"), Lauren Patel ("The Effects of Lying"), Sir Michael Palin ("Monty Python"), Sophie Willan ("Ludwig"), Jon Pointing ("Big Boys") and Paul Kaye ("Game of Thrones").

Following the premiere of the first two episodes, new episodes will be released every Wednesday through 4 November.

Here is the synopsis of "Small Prophets" provided by Apple TV+:

"Small Prophets" tells the comic story of the eccentric Michael Sleep (Pearce Quigley). Since the disappearance of his beloved Clea seven years ago, he has led a remarkably uneventful life — working at a hardware store, visiting his father Brian (Sir Michael Palin), and hoping for Clea's return. One day, Brian shares with him an ancient formula combining rainwater, horse manure, and a touch of alchemy. Armed with this recipe and a healthy dose of doubt, Michael sets about creating homunculi — mysterious spirits capable of foretelling the future — hoping they can answer the question on his mind: "Will I see Clea again?" In the process, he receives help from his young colleague Kacey (Lauren Patel). This unlikely friendship is fuelled, in part (though not entirely) of, by a shared disdain for branch manager Gordon (Mackenzie Crook). And their friendship draws the ire and curiosity of a pair of nosy neighbours (Sophie Willan, Jon Pointing) — neighbours who are determined to find out exactly what is going on inside the garden shed.
